item.title: Tsukuba Space Center: Japan's Gateway to Space — Guide
item.description: Tsukuba Space Center, operated by JAXA (the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency), is the country’s primary space development facility and one of the highlights of Tsukuba’s broader identity as a planned ‘science city.’ The centre’s free exhibition hall displays a full-size H-II rocket, mock-ups of the International Space Station’s Japanese Kibo module, satellite models and artefacts from Japan’s space history, while guided tours (some requiring advance reservation) take visitors past the mission control room used for real satellite and ISS operations.
